title: ExamAI extracted past paper
description: One past paper, split into individually addressable questions and tagged to syllabus units at import time. Extends the shape already emitted by examai-ingest/src/p2_extract.py; every field that existed there is preserved.

subject_code.description: Official Purbanchal University BIT code, and it MUST match a subject_code in units.sem<N>.json. The demo fixtures used invented codes such as 'BIT415AI'; semester 6 Artificial Intelligence is BIT351CO. A code absent from the unit vocabulary is a hard failure, not a warning — it means questions cannot be tagged.

full_marks.description: Total marks printed on the paper. Must equal the sum of groups[].marks_total.

curriculum.description: Which curriculum this paper belongs to. Derive it from the SUBJECT CODE, not from the printed header label: sem-6 BIT351CO-BIT356CO are new_course, and older codes (BIT370CO, BIT371CO, BIT376CO...) are old_course. A printed '(New Course)' is unreliable evidence — 2022 old-curriculum papers print it too, because the label was relative to a still earlier revision. This matters because old and new share subject NAMES: measured against the current BIT353CO units, the 2022 BIT371CO Data Mining paper fits only 62% clearly, and six of those fits land on a single unit. Pooling the two would skew that unit and add nothing elsewhere.

groups.description: The paper's sections and — critically — their choice rules. PU papers are not 'answer everything': a 2025 BIT351CO paper reads 'Group A: Answer TWO questions, 2x12=24' over three printed questions, and 'Group B: Answer SEVEN questions, 7x8=56' over eight. Marks alone cannot express that, which is why coverage is counted in QUESTIONS PER GROUP, not summed marks. A complete extraction of that Group B holds 8 questions worth 64 marks while the group is worth 56 — correct, not over-extracted.

questions_printed.description: How many questions the paper prints in this group — the number a complete extraction must contain.

answer_count.description: How many the candidate must answer. Equals questions_printed when there is no choice.

source_files.description: Page images this paper was extracted from, in reading order. Kept so the original layout can be shown to the student beside the text.

coverage.description: Makes incomplete extraction VISIBLE. Without it, a run that captured a third of a paper looks identical to a complete one — which is exactly what the demo fixtures did: 26 of 80 marks, every question 'high' confidence, extraction_notes empty. Counted in QUESTIONS PER GROUP because choice-based papers make summed marks meaningless as a completeness signal.

by_group.description: One entry per group in `groups`, in the same order.

status.description: complete: every group has questions_extracted == questions_printed. partial: at least one group has fewer — pages missed, questions merged, or OCR dropped a section. over_extracted: some group has more, which usually means one question was split into two.

missing_ranges.description: Best-effort note of what appears absent, e.g. 'Group B Q7-Q9'.

group.description: Section on the paper — A (short), B (medium), C (long) in the PU BIT format.

marks.description: Marks for this question. May be null ONLY on a sub-part whose share is not printed — many papers give a total and leave the split implicit. Inventing a division there would put fabricated numbers into mark-weight analysis; 0 would be worse, because it reads as a real value.

text.description: The printed question text. May be null in exactly two cases: the question is a bare stem whose entire content lives in its sub_parts (a paper's 'Q3 (a)... (b)...' with no sentence of its own), or the text was unreadable — and in that second case confidence must be 'low'. The validator rejects a null text with neither sub_parts nor low confidence, so 'null' can never quietly mean 'we lost it'.

question_type.description: Drives everything downstream. 'numerical' is the one that must NOT be served as a stored solution — topics repeat but numbers don't, so numerical questions get variant generation instead. 'diagram' means the answer requires one, which affects both generation and grading.

units.description:
Syllabus units this question tests. Tagged AT IMPORT, never at query time. More than one is normal and allowed — forcing a single unit loses the cross-topic questions that are exactly the ones worth counting.

May be EMPTY, but only alongside needs_review: true (the validator enforces the pair). An empty list is a real signal, not a failure: BIT353CO 2026 asks about multilayer feedforward networks versus a single-layer perceptron, and none of that subject's six syllabus units covers neural networks. Forcing the closest tag would have put a wrong question into a frequency count and made the syllabus look complete. An untagged, flagged question says the vocabulary needs checking — which is the more useful truth.

unit_id.description: MUST exist in units.sem<N>.json for this subject. Generated by scripts/dump-syllabus-units.ts from the syllabus the app already shows students, so the tagging vocabulary cannot drift from it.

tagged_by.description: A human tag outranks a model tag and must never be silently overwritten by a re-run.

marking_scheme.description: The checklist a grader compares against — key points and the marks each carries. Deliberately NOT a model answer: grading becomes 'which points are present, missing, wrong', which is how real examiners work and far more reliable than asking a model to score from feeling. The point marks should sum to the question's marks; where they cannot, say why in `notes`.

required.description: false for 'any four of the following' style alternatives.

solution_path.description: Relative path to the markdown solution — one source of truth for both the AI's context and what the student reads. Absent until batch generation has run. Never populated for question_type 'numerical'.

sub_parts.description: Parts (a), (b), (c). A parent carrying sub-parts should record its own marks as the sum of theirs.

choose.description: Set only for WITHIN-question choice, e.g. 'Write short notes on Any TWO:' followed by three options as sub_parts — that question carries choose: 2. Group-level choice ('Answer SEVEN questions') belongs in groups[].answer_count, not here. When `choose` is set, the sub-part marks sum to choose x (marks of one sub-part), not to all of them.

source_page.description: 1-indexed index into source_files, so the original layout can be shown beside the text.

confidence.description: Extraction confidence for the question TEXT specifically — not for its tagging, which carries its own per-unit confidence.

needs_review.description: True until a human has checked this question. Nothing publishes to students while true. Set it true automatically for: confidence below high, any low-confidence unit tag, a marking_scheme whose marks do not sum, and every question on a paper whose coverage.status is not 'complete'.

notes.description: Why this question needs review, or anything a reviewer should know — an ambiguous unit tag, unreadable marks, a question that spans a page break. A needs_review flag with no reason costs the reviewer the time it was meant to save.

diagram_description.description: One short phrase describing a figure, circuit or table the question depends on. Paired with has_diagram.
